summary: The tracker entity page covers CanonicalTracker, a library piece for state a scene keeps, such as a character's health or a party's roster, kept as data and never code. A tracker has a name, a description, a layout of record or list, typed fields, a note telling the model how to update it, an optional macro template for its prompt line, an optional icon and a change style the Messenger draws. The page explains the field rules shared with tools and held in one small module the decoder and the core both use, including a number's top taken from another field and field icons from the shipped glyph set, the absence of product limits beyond hostile-input ceilings, the two layouts, how the state lives in two scene-state slot families, how a scene links trackers, gets a Trackers block the budget measures and never cuts, and can switch change visuals off, the tracker macro, the single update_trackers tool, which applies a batch all or nothing and writes only deltas on the reply being written, and the read that answers what each reply changed. The Editing section describes the tracker editor, with its settings, the field editor a tool shares, and a rail showing what the AI gets, and says the Messenger's Trackers panel links, shows and edits them and that each reply shows what it changed in the style the tracker chose.

sections.title: Fields
sections.summary: A field has a name of a lowercase letter then lowercase letters, digits and underscores up to the providers' sixty-four character rule, a description, and a type of text, number, boolean or choice. The name rule, types and choices rule are shared with a tool's fields. A choice field has unique choices. A number field may have a min and a max, or instead take its top from another number field of the same tracker through maxField, which the decoder refuses when it names no field, a non-number, itself, a loop, or comes with max. A value above such a top is brought down to it, never refused, the top settled first, and a write that moves a top stores the clamped dependents in the same batch, so stored equals read; a top below min leaves the min. A field may have a well-formed icon id, not checked against the glyph table, a tracker an icon and a change style the Messenger draws; and any field a default that must fit. There are no product limits beyond the hostile-input ceilings.

sections.title: Layouts
sections.summary: A record is one set of fields. A list is rows, each keyed by a text name that is not blank and any length, holding every field; the name key is reserved on a list, so no list field is called name. A new row starts from the fields' defaults. The model finds a row whatever the case of the name it gives, and a row keeps the name it was made with, because the state folds by the exact name. The layout decides which slot family holds the tracker's state, so a record and a list never share one.

sections.title: State
sections.summary: A linked tracker keeps its state in a scene-state slot: tracker-record followed by the piece id uses the fields strategy with one delta per field, and tracker-list followed by the piece id uses the keyed-list strategy with one delta per row. These are two slot families declared once, and the store only folds them. Every shape check lives in the core tracker module, which knows the piece: trackerValue reads the current value with defaults filled, and a value that does not fit its field reads as the field's default. Because a write is a delta on the reply version being written, a regenerate, swipe, cut and fork all leave the tracker where the shown history says.

sections.title: In a scene
sections.summary: A scene links trackers by id in its prompting, in order without duplicates. A turn reads each through the tracker kind's strict decoder and leaves out one that is gone, fails the decoder, or whose name another linked tracker has. The prompt carries one system block headed Trackers right after the Props block, every turn, with each tracker's text: its template run read-only in the turn's macro pass, with its errors in the macro report, or the default rendering. Values the model wrote sit on one line, nothing is cut, and the budget measures the block so a tight window drops history. Templates read each other whatever the order, and the tracker macro reads the same state. The scene's trackerChanges switch turns the change visuals under each reply off, which the Messenger reads; only an off switch is stored. The Messenger's Trackers panel links and unlinks trackers, draws each value at the take's tip and edits it as the tool's own update, written as message-level deltas on the tip message.

sections.title: The update tool
sections.summary: When Narrator Tool Access is on, the connection takes tools and the turn is not a Continue, a scene with linked trackers offers one tool, update_trackers, taking updates each naming a tracker with an optional row, remove flag and set object. Its description is one fixed sentence plus one line per tracker with every field's type, range or choices and meaning, and the note, never cut, naming a top taken from another field as in hp from zero to hp_max. Items apply in order and the batch is all or nothing; a number past its range or such a top is clamped. The model is answered with only what changed. The deltas join the turn's pending set through a door for tracker slots only with no size cap, and the loop runs the tool as the one stateScoped write, exempt from answer shortening and a spent budget.

sections.title: What a reply changed
sections.summary: A read route answers, for a take and a range of its live messages, what each message changed in the library trackers on the version it shows, with each tracker's name, style and icons. A record's change is a field with its value before and after, and a list's is a row, added, changed or removed, with the whole row. Values are exact, never cut. It is one forward pass: the store's range read gives the state before the first message and each message's deltas in fold order, and the state is folded forward, so a person's edit shows as a change on its message, choosing another version shows that version's changes, and a cut message drops out. Only an unreadable piece is reported by its id with the stored values, a changed layout keeps the name and style, past lines are read through the current piece, only tracker slots are loaded, a missing branch or message is a 404, a malformed to a 400, an empty to the tip.

sections.title: Editing
sections.summary: A tracker opens in the Workbench's tracker editor: the shared header, which says in how many scenes it is linked and lists them on a click, an Identity and settings disclosure (what it tracks, how the AI should update it, shape, icon, how a reply shows changes, and an optional prompt line in macros), and the fields in the field editor a tool shares. A number's To can be a number, another number field, or none. The rail shows the Trackers block as prompt assembly renders it at the starting values, its plain line, its token cost, and the tracker's update tool line. A rename is followed a keystroke at a time from the name it began with, in other fields' tops and in the prompt line's macros, so a name typed through on the way takes nothing; renaming the tracker rewrites its macros. A draft the decoder refuses, or a prompt line whose macros fail, is not saved and is explained in plain words. Linking is the Trackers panel's; replies show changes as set here.
